newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART ROW, COTTBUS RELAX BEFORE CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART ROW, COTTBUS RELAX BEFORE CUP.

text.p: Favourites VfB Stuttgart and newly promoted second division club Cottbus Energie go into Saturday's German Cup final in very different moods.

Stuttgart, who finished fourth in the Bundesliga last season, have been distracted by internal rows and Cottbus players plan to add a further distraction on the pitch -- they've dyed their hair bright colours.
Stuttgart strikers Fredi Bobic and Giovane Elber have recently poured scorn on their side.

Brazilian Elber, playing his last match for Stuttgart before moving to league champions Bayern Munich next season, criticised the club's management, citing that as one of the reasons he had decided to quit the club for Bayern.
German international Bobic, who scored 19 of Stuttgart's 78 goals last season, slammed the club for not telling him about a reputed transfer offer from Spain's Real Betis.
"I will not let myself be treated like dirt," Bobic said.

The 25-year-old striker toned down his statement after talks with Stuttgart general director Ulrich Schaefer, who said the row had been the result of a misunderstanding and denied Betis had made an offer for Bobic.
Betis are known to be in the market for a strike partner for Spanish international Alfonso Perez, but have not made any official comment about Bobic.

Midfielder Matthias Hagner called on his teammates to stop arguing and concentrate on the final at Berlin's Olympic stadium, in front of a 75,800 sell-out crowd. "If we lose this game we will be the fools of the nation," Hagner said.

Meanwhile, Cottbus, promoted to the second division after the best season of their 31-year history, prepared to give the final a carnival atmosphere, several players dyeing their hair bright colours for the occasion.

Cottbus became the first team from former communist East Germany to reach the German final and only the second regional league club in history to get that far -- emulating Hertha Berlin's effort in 1993 -- when they beat first division Karlsruhe 3-0 in April.
"It will be the easiest game in the world. We will tackle this in a relaxed and comical way," said Cottbus coach Eduard Geyer after his club was promoted.

"Our chances are around 10 percent, but we'll use those to the full. Stuttgart have had a hard time in the Bundesliga against smaller teams like Duisburg or Duesseldorf," said Geyer, former coach of East Germany's national team.
"If we keep the scoreline to zero for long enough, they will get nervous," Cottbus's Jens Melzig said.
But Stuttgart, who have not won the Cup since 1958, are impatient for a win after leading the Bundesliga in March before falling away at the end of the season.
"We have waited long enough. The team are well prepared and very concentrated," said Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew.

Stuttgart - 1 Franz Wohlfahrt, 14 Thomas Schneider, 5 Frank Verlaat, 4 Thomas Berthold, 7 Matthias Hagner, 20 Zvonimir Soldo, 10 Krasimir Balakov, 16 Gerhard Poschner, 3 Thorsten Legat, 9 Giovane Elber, 11 Fredi Bobic.

Cottbus - 1 Kay Wehner, 3 Thomas Hossmang, 4 Sven Benken, 5 Jens Melzig, 7 Ingo Schneider, 6 Detlev Irrgang, 21 Willi Kronhardt, 8 Jens-Uwe Zoephel, 14 Jorg Woltmann, 9 Toralf Konetzke, 17 Frank Seifert.
